open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict (M08)
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict” conflicts with “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions” and with the meaning facts `trial_executions` and `decided_at`.
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against the unchanged corpus, is the prior AdmissionVerdict returned, or is a new verdict record created for the new trial executions?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and do not run another admission
Create a distinct AdmissionVerdict for every admission run
Run again but replace or amend the existing verdict's evidence
open_points.default_guess: Create a distinct immutable verdict record for every admission run.

open_points.subject: ProofResult (M17)
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result” conflicts with “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).”
open_points.question: What distinguishes two ProofResults for the same immutable flow version when an external proof dependency, such as a binding's acceptance status, changes?
options: ProofResult identity includes a snapshot or digest of all proof dependencies
ProofResult is an unidentifiable transient observation and may differ for the same version
The first ProofResult is permanent and later binding changes cannot alter it
open_points.default_guess: Treat ProofResult as a transient result identified by the flow version plus the proof-dependency snapshot.

open_points.subject: Capture failed execution into TrialCase (M06, M19, M22)
open_points.text: Capture refuses an execution “whose run was already released (its files are gone),” but “a file moves between nodes through a spool that belongs to its run and is emptied when the run ends — except a `failed` run,” so files are also gone after a run ends `refused`, `cancelled` or `succeeded` without ever being released.
open_points.question: May a failed function execution be captured after its run ends in a status other than `failed`, and does eligibility differ between value-only inputs and inputs containing spooled files?
options: Allow capture whenever all required inputs still exist; value-only executions remain capturable but file executions require a live or failed-unreleased spool
Allow capture only while the run is active or is failed and unreleased
Allow every otherwise eligible capture after any run ending, requiring file bytes to be retained or copied
open_points.default_guess: Allow capture when all inputs still exist: value-only inputs remain capturable, while file inputs require the run's spool still to exist.

open_points.subject: Installation (M28)
open_points.text: “Identity: value” and “equal configuration is the same installation” conflict with one installation continuing while “the token list is read again whenever it has changed” and while the owner may change the configured manifest revision.
open_points.question: Is an installation a stable entity whose configuration can change, or is each distinct configuration value a different installation?
options: Installation is a stable entity and its configuration has successive value snapshots
Every configuration change creates a different Installation value
Only token changes preserve installation identity; other configuration changes create a new installation
open_points.default_guess: Model the installation as a stable entity and its configuration as replaceable snapshots.

open_points.subject: Implementation inspection and repair context (K-11, K-12, M05)
open_points.text: The surface has an action to “inspect functions,” while M05 says code is “shown to the agent repairing its slot” and K-12 says “For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence,” but no repair-reading action or criterion for being “repairing” is defined.
open_points.question: Which product action may return implementation source, to which actors, and for which implementations?
options: Inspecting a named slot returns only its current implementation source and repair evidence
General function inspection may return any stored implementation source
Only an author-capable agent may request a dedicated repair view; ordinary inspection omits source
The owner may inspect all source, while agents receive only the current implementation of one named slot
open_points.default_guess: Treat inspection of one named slot as the repair view and return only that slot's current implementation source and evidence.

open_points.subject: EffectAttempt after an unsent draft-write (M26)
open_points.text: A `draft-write` attempt records “the flow activation under which the run started” as its authority, but the lifecycle says without qualification: “A `not_sent` attempt leaves its approval unused (M24), so a resume sends a new attempt under it.”
open_points.question: Under what authority is a `draft-write` retried after its attempt ended `not_sent`, given that its original authority was a flow activation rather than an approval?
options: Retry under the same pinned flow activation
Require a fresh EffectApproval before retrying
Create a new attempt under whichever authority is currently available
open_points.default_guess: Retry under the same flow activation because no send occurred and the fresh-approval exception applies only after `not_applied`.
